title: When is a System Discoverable from Data? Discovery Requires Chaos
summary: Argues theoretically, in spaces of continuous and analytic vector fields, that chaos (systems chaotic everywhere on their domain, e.g. Lorenz) makes governing equations uniquely recoverable from a single trajectory, whereas systems with conserved quantities (first integrals) are not analytically identifiable and non-chaotic systems generally require extra physical priors beyond the trajectory.

title: Discovering governing equations from data by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) 113(15), 3932-3937
summary: Introduces SINDy: builds a library of candidate nonlinear functions of the state and uses sparse regression to select the few active terms, exploiting the fact that most physical governing equations are sparse in a suitable function basis; recovery is conditional on the true dynamics lying within the candidate library span and on accurate derivative estimation.

title: Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics with Control (SINDYc)
venue: arXiv preprint (related: Kaiser, Kutz, Brunton, Proc. R. Soc. A 474(2219), 2018)
summary: Extends SINDy to systems with exogenous control/forcing inputs, demonstrated on Lotka-Volterra and forced Lorenz systems; relevant to whether active experimental design/actuation can restore identifiability in non-chaotic regimes.

title: Weak SINDy for Partial Differential Equations
summary: Reformulates SINDy regression in weak/integral form using test functions instead of pointwise derivatives, giving orders-of-magnitude better robustness to measurement noise and avoiding explicit numerical differentiation, which otherwise can leak spurious structure into recovered equations.

title: Weak-form modified sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics
venue: arXiv preprint / Journal of Computational Physics
summary: Combines weak-form SINDy (WSINDy) with modified SINDy (mSINDy) to simultaneously identify parsimonious dynamics and extract noise probability distributions via automatic differentiation, improving accuracy and noise characterization under relatively strong noise.

title: Ensemble-SINDy: Robust sparse model discovery in the low-data, high-noise limit, with active learning and control
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society A 478(2260), 20210904
summary: Applies bootstrap aggregation (bagging) over SINDy fits from data subsets to compute per-term inclusion probabilities, enabling uncertainty-quantified and probabilistic model discovery; demonstrates recovery under roughly twice the noise levels previously reported, useful for quantifying ambiguity rather than binary recovery.

title: Benchmarking sparse system identification with low-dimensional chaos
summary: Large-scale benchmark of four SINDy optimizer variants across the Gilpin dysts standardized database of chaotic systems; finds strong performance from the original sequential-thresholded-least-squares algorithm and a mixed-integer variant, and shows weak-form SINDy improves results even on clean data.

title: AI Feynman: a Physics-Inspired Method for Symbolic Regression
summary: Combines neural-network fitting with physics-inspired simplification heuristics (symmetry, separability, compositionality) in a recursive symbolic-regression algorithm; recovered all 100 Feynman-Lectures equations versus 71 for prior tools and raised success on a harder benchmark from 15% to 90%, while noting symbolic regression is NP-hard in general.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Science with PySR and SymbolicRegression.jl
summary: Describes PySR, a Python front-end to the SymbolicRegression.jl backend implementing a multi-population evolutionary evolve-simplify-optimize search over symbolic expressions with distributed compute, intended as a practical scientific symbolic-regression tool.

title: gplearn: Genetic Programming in Python, with a scikit-learn inspired API
summary: Scikit-learn-compatible genetic-programming symbolic regressor (SymbolicRegressor); a lightweight, widely used baseline for symbolic regression, often compared against more elaborate tools like PySR.

title: A Data-Driven Approximation of the Koopman Operator: Extending Dynamic Mode Decomposition
summary: Introduces Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD): approximates Koopman operator eigenvalues, eigenfunctions, and modes from snapshot pairs and a dictionary of scalar observables, without requiring explicit governing equations or an integrator.

title: On Convergence of Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition to the Koopman Operator
summary: Establishes conditions (dictionary richness, sampling) under which EDMD's finite-dictionary approximation provably converges to the true, possibly infinite-dimensional, Koopman operator -- a formal sufficient-condition result analogous to the identifiability conditions this project seeks in a restricted function class.

title: Observability and Structural Identifiability of Nonlinear Biological Systems
summary: Tutorial/review using differential-geometry tools to jointly analyze observability (recovering internal state from outputs) and structural identifiability (uniquely determining parameters from noise-free output data given the model structure alone), providing the formal vocabulary distinguishing structural from practical (data-limited) non-identifiability.

title: Koopman Operators for Generalized Persistence of Excitation Conditions for Nonlinear Systems
summary: Reformulates persistent excitation (PE) conditions -- the standard requirement that regressors span enough of state/input space over time for parameter estimates to converge uniquely -- using Koopman operators, including for fixed versus designed initial conditions; a candidate formal mechanism for why chaotic trajectories might satisfy PE-like richness conditions that periodic or quasiperiodic trajectories do not.

title: Let's Do the Time-Warp-Attend: Learning Topological Invariants of Dynamical Systems
summary: Addresses learning topological invariants and conjugacy classes of dynamical systems; illustrates that two vector fields related by a coordinate change (topological conjugacy, h∘f = g∘h) produce indistinguishable trajectories up to relabeling of state variables -- a structural, exact mechanism for non-identifiability relevant to constructing adversarial coordinate-transform counterexamples.

title: Lorenz-like chaos in NH3-FIR lasers
venue: In: Time Series Prediction: Forecasting the Future and Understanding the Past (A. S. Weigend, N. A. Gershenfeld, eds.), Santa Fe Institute Studies in the Sciences of Complexity, Proc. Vol. XV, Addison-Wesley, pp. 73-104
summary: Source and physical documentation of the Santa Fe Time Series Prediction Competition's Dataset A: a scalar intensity time series digitized from a real far-infrared NH3 ring-laser experiment. The authors document that the laser's intensity pulsations share dimension, entropy, and autocorrelation-decay features with numerically generated Lorenz-equation data, i.e. the physical system is modeled by the Lorenz-Haken equations (a 3-variable system isomorphic to the Lorenz equations) and independently classified as chaotic in this original source -- used in this project (NEXT_STEPS.md item #9, PROJECT_CHARTER.md's bounded real-world-data amendment) as the one permitted real-world benchmark to test whether the SINDy pipeline's synthetic chaos-vs-control findings transfer to genuine experimental data with no known closed-form ground truth. Data obtained via a Wayback Machine mirror of the original host (see DECISION_LOG.md, scripts/download_santafe_laser.py) since the live page is offline.
